# Thursday 10 September 2026

## Data governance board: consortium clause not adopted

The board discussed [[data-access-policy-draft-3|draft 3]] of the [[data-access-policy-revision|Data Access Policy Revision]] for about fifty minutes and did not adopt it. There was support for the principle. The conditions are a DPIA that covers the receiving sites, the registry's written position on linked outcomes, and tighter deletion wording. Everything is in the [[data-governance-board-2026-09-10|board note]]. It comes back on 12 November.

I declared my interest at the start, since my own group benefits first through the Halo validation for the [[mrd-manuscript|MRD Manuscript]], and did not vote. Not everyone accepted my argument that federated analysis cannot replace a locked-model validation the journal will audit; that disagreement is kept in [[should-halo-validation-run-federated-instead-of-transfer|Should Halo validation run federated instead of transfer?]].

## Lab meeting after the summer

The morning [[lab-meeting-2026-09-10|lab meeting]] was mostly operations. Kestrel stops taking jobs next week, and unowned directories will be archived by default ([[kestrel-data-inventory|Kestrel data inventory]]). We still have no GPU partition on Halyard, so Amara's segmentation pauses after the Kestrel cut-off. Postdoc interviews are next week, and Sofia's [[sofia-thesis-committee|committee]] is set for November.

## Where this leaves the revision

The earliest the clause can be adopted is mid-November. The revision timeline now assumes it will be, which leaves little slack for the validation analysis.
